# seashells.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/seashells.py`*

## Overview

`seashells.py` is the sea_eco integration shim. It provides a `SEASerializable` base class to all rayTEM objects that need to serialize to/from `.sea` files. The module detects at load time whether sea_eco is installed and exposes one of two implementations:

- **sea_eco present:** `SEASerializable` wraps `pySEA.sea_eco.architecture.base_structure.SEASerializable`. The `to_sea` and `from_sea` overrides add rayTEM-specific logic before delegating to the parent.
- **sea_eco absent:** `SEASerializable` is a no-op stub that prints warnings on any `.sea` call. `Microscope`, `MicroscopeSection`, and all `Element` subclasses inherit this class regardless, so their interface is consistent whether or not sea_eco is present.

This is the **only module in the rayTEM package that imports from sea_eco**. All sea_eco coupling is localized here.

---

## Module-level variables

### `sea_available`

Boolean set at import time. `True` if `pySEA.sea_eco.architecture.base_structure.SEASerializable` was found; `False` otherwise (import error is caught and printed as a warning, not raised).

---

## SEASerializable (sea_eco present)

Wraps the real `_SEASerializable` from sea_eco. All rayTEM objects that need serialization inherit from this class.

### `SEASerializable.to_sea(self, filename)`

Before calling `super().to_sea(filename)`, fills in any empty names on the object graph. sea_eco's serializer generates names like `"Drift_2"` for unnamed objects; instead we set them to `"None_Microscope"`, `"None_0"`, etc., so we can detect and clear them on reload without confusion with user-chosen names.

Handles two cases:
- Object has `self.sections` (is a `Microscope`): fills `self.name`, all section names, and all element names.
- Object has `self.elements` (is a `MicroscopeSection`): fills `self.name` and all element names.

### `SEASerializable.from_sea(self, filename)`

Calls `super().from_sea(filename)` to deserialize via sea_eco, then walks the restored object graph and re-casts each sub-object back to the appropriate rayTEM class via `safeReinstantiate`. This is necessary because sea_eco restores objects as plain `SEASerializable` instances — they will have the stored attributes but lack rayTEM methods like `propagate_ray`.

Also strips the `"None"` sentinel names back to empty strings.

---

## SEASerializable (sea_eco absent)

Stub class with `__init__`, `to_sea`, and `from_sea`. Each sea method prints a warning directing the user to install sea_eco or use `microscope.save` (JSON). The stub exists so that `Microscope` and friends can inherit `SEASerializable` unconditionally.

---

## Module-level functions

### `safeReinstantiate(source, cls)`

Re-casts a deserialized `SEASerializable` instance to the correct rayTEM typed class.

**Why this is needed:** sea_eco's `from_sea` reconstructs the object graph as bare `SEASerializable` instances. These carry all serialized attributes (`strength`, `length`, `position`, etc.) but are missing `propagate_ray`, `transfer_matrix`, and other rayTEM-specific methods. `safeReinstantiate` re-instantiates each object as the proper class.

**How it works:**
1. `cls` is a string like `"Drift"`, `"QLens"`, `"Section"`, or `"Microscope"` — taken from `source.kind` for elements or hard-coded for containers. A lookup table maps these strings to their Python classes.
2. Uses `inspect.signature(cls)` to find accepted `__init__` parameters, then filters `source.__dict__` to only those keys. This handles version mismatches where serialized objects may carry stale attributes that newer constructors no longer accept.
3. Returns `cls(**filtered_dict)` — a freshly constructed, fully functional rayTEM object.

The kind-to-class lookup:

| `kind` string | Class |
|---|---|
| `"Drift"` | `Drift` |
| `"QLens"`, `"Thin lens"` | `Lens` |
| `"Source"` | `Source` |
| `"Microscope"` | `Microscope` |
| `"Section"` | `MicroscopeSection` |
| `"Dipole"`, `"Thin dipole"` | `Dipole` |
| `"Quad"`, `"Thin quad"` | `Quadrapole` |

See [elements.md](elements.md) for how `kind` is set on each element. See [assemblies.md](assemblies.md) for the analogous `load_microscope` path which handles the same reconstruction for JSON-serialized microscopes.
